plants.name: Calluna vulgaris
plants.description: Wild moorlands in the Scottish Highlands turn into rolling carpets of pink-purple. Each wiry stem is covered in tiny bell-shaped blossoms. Bees swarm over them, and the hills hum in the late-summer light.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late July through September, peaking in mid-August to early September
plants.location: Highland moors and heathlands of Scotland and northern Europe
plants.funFact: Heather honey is prized for its thick, jelly-like texture. It is so gel-like that it must be pressed out of the comb instead of spun.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem bursts into clouds of fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms. They light up bushland at the end of winter. The branches look as if they are dusted with sunshine.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, roughly July to October, with a strong August–September display
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including South Australia, Victoria and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Australia celebrates National Wattle Day on September 1, and the golden wattle's green and gold colors are the country's official national colors.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall, sun-chasing stems carry broad golden-rayed faces with dark, seed-packed centers. Fields and gardens across the Northern Hemisphere glow with them in late summer. Goldfinches and bees crowd the heads.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer into early autumn, commonly July through September
plants.location: Native to North America; blooming in the Great Plains of the United States and in gardens and fields across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: What looks like one giant flower is really a head of hundreds of tiny individual florets. The seeds form in a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence.
